subject.title: feat(cron): shell precheck gate to skip LLM when no work

question: Should OpenClaw expose a separate persisted `job.precheck` host-shell gate, or should the existing cron trigger contract be extended to provide the canonical pre-payload admission interface?
rationale: Both choices create a durable operator-facing job schema and CLI contract. The contributor has identified different claimed runtime semantics, but repository policy requires maintainers to choose the public configuration surface rather than letting a parallel gate become permanent by implementation alone.

options.title: Define one canonical admission gate first
options.body: Pause merge until the cron owner specifies whether the existing trigger contract should be extended or a separate precheck contract is intentionally required, then align schema, CLI, docs, and tests to that decision.

options.title: Approve a separate precheck contract
options.body: Accept `precheck` only with an explicit scope for host-shell semantics, a documented relationship to triggers, upgrade/operator guidance, and persisted scheduler-to-history proof.

options.title: Narrow or pause the proposal
options.body: Keep the underlying cost-saving idea tracked while deferring the new persisted shell surface until the cron API direction is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Define one canonical admission gate first
recommendation.body: Pause merge until the cron owner specifies whether the existing trigger contract should be extended or a separate precheck contract is intentionally required, then align schema, CLI, docs, and tests to that decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal author can promptly reshape the branch after the cron API decision, although the actual contract choice requires a repository owner.
